exposure: Gut microbiota profiles (16S rRNA gene sequencing)
cohort: The study included 80 healthy pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who delivered at the study hospital between January 2022 and December 2023, stratified into CS (n=40) and vaginal delivery (VD, n=40) groups, matched for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, and gestational age.
finding: Gestational gut microbiota dysbiosis, metabolic dysregulation (higher pyruvic acid and lactate, lower phenylalanine), and increased CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and Tregs were significantly associated with an increased risk of Cesarean section.
mod_finding: Gestational gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic dysregulation were significantly associated with an increased risk of Cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Fecal samples were collected one month prior to delivery; serum and peripheral blood samples were also analyzed in relation to this period before delivery.
gest_age: Participants were matched for gestational age, but specific gestational ages of the babies are not provided.
